judged_text: When uniqueGuests.length === 0 after filtering, the handler throws TRPCError BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid", but that condition also covers the case where every requested guest already exists as an attendee. A user who retries after a partially-failed earlier request (attendees persisted, calendar/emails failed — see the no-rollback finding) gets 'emails must be unique and valid' even though their input is perfectly valid and unique; the wrong-shape, wrong-content error misdirects debugging and blocks the retry that would be needed to complete the calendar update and emails.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that already exist in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones. If the caller submits only emails that are already attendees (a valid, unique input), `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers `throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is a misleading error message for that case. However, the diff doesn’t establish expected idempotent retry semantics (i.e., whether re-adding existing guests should succeed), so it’s best framed as an edge-case/UX/API contract issue rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.
